Consider this worked case: A department might use this course to test a new AI ethics module before adding it to the standard curriculum. List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections. beats.narration: Now define Faculty Role and Customization precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. Specific course details (such as prerequisites, course topics, format, learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs) will be determined by the faculty member(s) who propose a specific seminar course in this area. Consider this worked case: An instructor could adapt the course to focus on cybersecurity, machine learning, or software engineering based on departmental needs. Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them. A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.

beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Cluster Classification operates in a concrete sequence. Specific course instances will be identified as belonging to no cluster; hence, such courses will count only as general Computer Science electives. Consider this worked case: Students can enroll in CSCI-509 to fulfill general elective requirements without meeting specific cluster prerequisites. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in ACM Ethics Foundation and make the decision criteria explicit. The ACM Code directs computing professionals to contribute to society and human well-being. Consider this worked case: Developing accessible software tools that help people with disabilities aligns with this ethical directive. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Present a circular diagram linking 'society' and 'human well-being' to core computing practices.

beats.narration: Apply Avoiding Harm and Honesty to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. Computing professionals should avoid harm. Consider this worked case: Auditing an algorithm for biased training data and correcting it prevents discriminatory outcomes in hiring tools. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Respecting Work and Privacy, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. They should respect the work required to produce new ideas and creative works. Consider this worked case: Citing open-source libraries properly and encrypting user data in a mobile application demonstrates these values. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Quality and Security Standards with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products. Consider this worked case: Implementing rigorous code reviews and automated testing ensures both reliable software and sustainable development workflows. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.

beats.narration: Use Responsible Technical Communication to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. It cites prior work and identifies the contribution being reported. Consider this worked case: A research paper clearly separates its novel algorithm from existing methods and explicitly states the new findings. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a two-column layout: left for 'claims/evidence', right for 'contributions/prior work' with arrows linking them.

beats.narration: Connect Methods and Results Integrity to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. Results should be reported accurately rather than selected to create a misleading conclusion. Consider this worked case: Publishing raw data alongside statistical analysis allows independent verification of experimental outcomes. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Illustrate a magnifying glass over a methodology section and a graph with clear, unaltered axes.

beats.narration: Finish with Research Integrity and Practical Analysis as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification. Consider this worked case: Using reference managers to track citations and disclosing funding sources maintains academic honesty in computer science research. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.

sources.excerpt: This course examines current topics in Computer Science. This is intended to allow faculty to pilot potential new undergraduate offerings. Specific course details (such as prerequisites, course topics, format, learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs) will be determined by the faculty member(s) who propose a specific seminar course in this area. Specific course instances will be identified as belonging to no cluster; hence, such courses will count only as general Computer Science electives. Contact Hours: Lecture/Lab 3
sources.title: RIT CSCI-509 Seminar in Computer Science catalog description

sources.author: Association for Computing Machinery
sources.excerpt: The ACM Code directs computing professionals to contribute to society and human well-being. Computing professionals should avoid harm. They should be honest and trustworthy. They should be fair and take action not to discriminate. They should respect the work required to produce new ideas and creative works. They should respect privacy. They should honor confidentiality. Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Robust security should be designed and implemented when appropriate. Ethical computing decisions identify stakeholders, foreseeable benefits and harms, uncertainty, alternatives, and obligations.
sources.title: ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct

sources.author: Association for Computing Machinery
sources.excerpt: Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence. It cites prior work and identifies the contribution being reported. Methods should be described well enough for readers to evaluate the work. Results should be reported accurately rather than selected to create a misleading conclusion. Limitations and threats to validity should be made visible. Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification. Conflicts and relevant relationships should be disclosed according to publication policy. A research project narrows a question, reviews literature, defines a reproducible method, evaluates results, and communicates for the intended audience.
